constraints.text: See how far to go. / Use will's straight edge, as the turning square or any arc may align at a proper point.
constraints.reading: Imagery of geometric alignment: a 'straight edge', a 'turning square' (a right-angle / corner), and an 'arc' that 'align at a proper point'. Spatially suggests sighting along a straight line and/or a curve to a precise convergence point - i.e., the spot is found where a straight bearing meets a curved feature (a bend, a curving ridge, an arc of trees, a sweeping view). A 'square' may also hint at a right-angled corner of rock or a man-made marker.

constraints.text: may align at a proper point
constraints.reading: A precise convergence/'point'. Could imply the hiding spot sits at a literal point/promontory or at the intersection of sightlines.

constraints.text: This is no imaginary wonderland. Now look.
constraints.reading: Explicit instruction that the described landscape is a REAL physical place, not metaphor. The spatial images (oaks, water, rock, height) should be taken literally as features one will see on site.

constraints.text: You can take your own path / an X leads the way / or simply follow shimmering circles of gold.
constraints.reading: Two navigation alternatives: an 'X' (a trail crossing/junction, an X-shaped blaze on a tree, or two paths intersecting) OR follow 'circles of gold'. The X reads as an on-site crossing or marker rather than a buried spot. Stand at or near a path intersection.

constraints.text: or simply follow shimmering circles of gold
constraints.reading: Round/circular gold-colored shimmering objects to follow as a trail. Most literal natural read: golden round leaves that shimmer/tremble (aspen-like trees turning gold). Could also be sun glinting in circles on water, or round gold lichen/markers. Color = gold/yellow; shape = round/circular; quality = shimmering/trembling.

constraints.text: There may be magic in the water, but the pike are rather all around.
constraints.reading: A water feature is present ('magic in the water' - possibly a spring, effervescent/mineral water, or sparkling/reflective water). But the dominant surrounding feature is 'pike' - readable as sharp-topped peaks/hills all around (a 'pike' = a pointed peak), i.e. the spot is ringed by peaked terrain. Water nearby, peaks surrounding.

constraints.text: the pike are rather all around
constraints.reading: Surrounded on multiple sides by pointed peaks/summits ('pike' = peak). The spot has peaks visible all around it - an encircled, mountainous vantage.

constraints.text: If you get warm, you may find shady oaks.
constraints.reading: Oak trees provide shade at or near the spot. A 'warmth' (proximity/'getting warm' in the hunt sense) cue is paired with oaks - the hiding place is at or beside oak trees offering shade. Feature: oak tree(s); the cache may be at the base of / under an oak.

constraints.text: When close, the haiku curls a little further on where few have seen it.
constraints.reading: When near the spot, something 'curls a little further on' - suggests a curving/winding path or feature that bends just beyond, in a hidden/seldom-visited place ('where few have seen it'). The final spot is slightly past a bend, off the beaten track, tucked away from common view.

constraints.text: where few have seen it
constraints.reading: The spot is hidden/secluded, rarely visited - not on an obvious overlook but tucked just out of sight.

constraints.text: And if you don't go down you may never know how high you ever want to be.
constraints.reading: Strong elevation cue: you must 'go down' to appreciate 'how high'. Implies a high place / overlook, possibly reached after descending (a spot below a high point, or a low approach to a high vantage). The hiding place is associated with height and a vertical relationship - go down then appreciate high, or the spot is high up.

constraints.text: And if you don't go down
constraints.reading: Directional cue to descend ('go down') at some stage of the approach - down a slope, into a valley/draw, or downhill from a high point.

constraints.text: how high you ever want to be
constraints.reading: The location is high / elevated - a high vantage point.

constraints.text: The sky smiles on you. Dancers are on the land.
constraints.reading: Open sky / clear view of the sky ('the sky smiles') implies an exposed, open spot with a broad view. 'Dancers are on the land' could be a feature whose shape/movement evokes dancing - swaying trees, wind-moved grass, moving rock formations, or a named land feature - on the ground around you.

constraints.text: And if you stay to see the night it will ignite with the flame of starlight.
constraints.reading: Open, dark-sky vantage where stars are vivid ('flame of starlight') - an unobstructed view of the night sky. Reinforces a high, open, exposed location away from light/obstruction.

constraints.text: or sat upon a rock, allowing nature's wide embrace to sustain their bliss
constraints.reading: A specific sitting ROCK is at the spot - one can sit upon it. 'Nature's wide embrace' = a wide, panoramic/sweeping view from that rock. The cache likely is at or beside a sittable rock with a broad outlook. Feature: a rock you can sit on; view: wide/panoramic.

constraints.text: nature's wide embrace
constraints.reading: A wide, expansive, encompassing view/vista from the spot - panoramic outlook.

constraints.text: if you spy others warming with the sunlight, or sat upon a rock
constraints.reading: A spot where other people sit/rest in the sun on a rock - suggests a recognized resting/overlook point that visitors use (a popular sitting rock or sunny ledge), implying an accessible vantage rather than deep wilderness.

constraints.text: Our conductor, as with a trace of a baton through the air, gives direction.
constraints.reading: A sweeping motion 'through the air' that 'gives direction' - faint imagery of a sweeping line/gesture pointing the way; possibly a sweeping arc/line across the landscape (a ridge line, a sweeping curve) that indicates a bearing.

constraints.text: Postscript: No treasure is hidden more than three miles from any road; reaching a box should take no more than a couple of hours, usually far less.
constraints.reading: Hard spatial constraint: hiding spot is within 3 miles of a road and reachable in under ~2 hours on foot. Bounds the search radius from any trailhead/road to a single-day, short on-foot distance.

constraints.text: Postscript: treasure boxes are NOT BURIED - they are hidden; no shovel or metal detector; no digging.
constraints.reading: Surface cache, not underground. The spot is a place to TUCK/HIDE an object on the surface - e.g., a rock crevice, under a ledge, in a hollow, at the base of a tree, behind/under a boulder. Look for a natural surface concealment.

constraints.text: Postscript: none under water (no raft/canoe, no swift current); never wade or cross high water.
constraints.reading: Spot is on dry land near but not in water. Any 'water' imagery means water is adjacent/visible, not something you must enter or cross. Constrains the spot to the bank/shore side, accessible without water crossing.

constraints.text: Postscript: none requiring scaling a cliff or rock face; no climbing.
constraints.reading: Even though the spot is 'high', it does NOT require climbing a cliff or rock face. The high vantage is reached by walking/trail, not by scaling - so a ledge/overlook accessible on foot, not a vertical wall.

constraints.text: Postscript: all outdoors (not inside structures); on open/public land.
constraints.reading: The hiding spot is an outdoor natural feature, not a building/structure interior. Look for natural landmarks (rock, tree, ledge), not man-made enclosures.

constraints.text: Dust-jacket near-haiku referenced in poem: 'Be solid, have grit; / sparkle even as you pine. / Here lies a joy divined.'
constraints.reading: Material/texture imagery: 'solid', 'grit' (gritty stone, e.g. a coarse/granular rock surface), 'sparkle' (crystalline/glittering rock or mineral), and 'pine' (pine trees nearby, or 'pine' as longing). Suggests the spot involves a solid, gritty, sparkling rock and possibly pine trees. 'Here lies' hints the cache is AT this described feature.

constraints.text: Viking gold ring motif: 'dozens of circles stamped into eight serpentine forms.'
constraints.reading: Shape echo (speculative): circles arranged in winding/serpentine (snaking) forms. Could metaphorically echo a winding, snaking path/switchbacks or a serpentine ridge/creek bend with rounded features - a curving, coiling landform. Tag low: this is an object description, not a stated place.

constraints.text: Andvari/serpentine asides: cursed gold guarded by a serpent-dragon in a valley.
constraints.reading: Speculative thematic shape: a valley with serpentine/winding character (a coiling creek, serpentine switchbacks, or a snake-like ridge). Suggests checking for a valley/draw with winding water or trail near the spot. Low confidence - thematic, not stated.

constraints.text: Southeast Asian gold box carved with a deer (front) and a chicken (back).
constraints.reading: Object with directional front/back faces (deer front, chicken/bird back) - very weak speculative echo of an oriented marker having a 'front' facing one direction. Negligible spatial value.

constraints.text: Tanzanite called perfect for a 'dazzling pendant'; recurring pendant/necklace + 'circles of gold' motif across items and poem.
constraints.reading: Recurring round/looping 'pendant', 'necklace', 'circle', 'ring' shapes. Speculative: the spot's defining feature may be circular/looping (a ring of rocks, a circular clearing, a loop in a trail or stream, a rounded knob). Tag low - motif convergence only.
